sources.entry: Opengist - Pastebin powered by Git. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker/Go/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Opengist is a self-hosted Pastebin powered by Git, where snippets are stored in Git repositories and can be managed via Git or a web interface.
summary.what_it_does: Opengist lets you create and share code or text snippets that are each backed by a Git repository. Snippets can be cloned, pulled and pushed with standard Git commands over HTTP or SSH, or edited through the web UI. It offers public, unlisted and private snippets, syntax highlighting with markdown and CSV support, and code search across snippets. Users can browse other users' snippets, likes and forks, add topics, embed snippets in other sites, and view revision history. Raw files and ZIP downloads are available, and login can use OAuth2 with GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, or OpenID Connect.
use_cases: host a private GitHub Gist alternative
share snippets with a team over Git
embed code snippets in other websites
store notes or config fragments with revision history
how_to_run: Create docker-compose.yml mapping ports 6157 (HTTP) and 2222 (SSH) with a volume at /opengist
Or download the release binary for your system, extract it, and run ./opengist
From source: git clone the repo, cd opengist, run make, then ./opengist
notable: Every snippet is a real Git repository, so standard Git clone, pull and push work
Supports SSH and HTTP Git access alongside the web interface
OAuth2 login with GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, and OpenID Connect
Helm chart and Docker images are provided
caveats: Building from source requires Git 2.28+, Go 1.23+ and Node.js 16+
Development environment setup is described in a separate run-development.md file
